sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Tunnel-forming phenotype in 3D acini stimulated earlier than GFP-alone control (functional activity preserved); surface display confirmed by anti-GFP antibody staining of non-permeabilized GFP-PODXL-expressing acini (L3).
sites.rationale: PODXL has a single extracellular N-terminus (residues 23–460) and a single intracellular C-terminus; the signal peptide (residues 1–22) is cleaved co-translationally. The paper explicitly states the GFP is extracellular and the construct is named GFP-PODXL (GFP prefix), leaving exactly one possible junction: after residue 22 (last SP residue, S) and before residue 23 (mature N-terminus, S). Python confirmed res(22)='S' and res(23)='S'. The junction is 438 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. Canine ortholog GP135 tagged with myc-SNAP at the same N-terminal position (L7) independently corroborates this junction. Full-length, membrane-anchored GFP-PODXL (isoform A) expressed in PC3 cells via retroviral vector. The paper explicitly labels the construct 'extracellularly GFP-tagged PODXL', confirming the GFP is on the extracellular face. PODXL is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein (N-out, C-in); the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 22. The construct name 'GFP-PODXL' (GFP prefix) is consistent with an N-terminal fusion placed after the signal peptide.

sources.claim: Expression of extracellularly green fluorescent protein (GFP)–tagged PODXL [isoform A; henceforth described as wild type (WT)] in PC3 cells stimulated the tunnel-forming phenotype to occur earlier at the expense of local spreading compared to GFP alone (GFP-PODXL; fig.

literature_notes: L7 (PMC12497838) reports a myc-SNAP fusion to canine GP135 (podocalyxin ortholog) expressed in MDCK cells, which maps to the same N-terminal extracellular junction (after SP cleavage) as L2. Because it is the same junction, it is not a separate site; it is indirect corroboration. L5/L6 (PMC1796660) describe a ΔEC chimeric construct in which CD43's signal peptide plus a FLAG tag replaces 'most of Podocalyxin's extracellular domain'; this is a domain-swap experiment, not a tag insertion at a defined residue within full-length PODXL, so no junction can be pinned and it does not qualify as a site. L4 (PMC9897673) reports K431R, K525R, K526R, K547R mutagenesis within the GFP-PODXL backbone; these are mutagenesis positions, not tag-insertion sites, and are recorded in other_positions.
